reason: E1 supports the general need for post-process heat treatment in AM HEAs, and E2 supports that low-to-moderate temperature annealing reduces residual stress without major phase changes. However, neither passage provides evidence for in situ laser-induced annealing, its ability to homogenize grain structure, or the effectiveness of real-time temperature monitoring in this context.
premises: Post-process heat treatment is essential to optimize AM-fabricated HEA microstructures and mechanical properties
Annealing at low to moderate temperatures (300–500 °C) can reduce internal stresses and dislocation density without significant phase transformations or coarsening
In situ laser-induced annealing can provide controlled thermal energy to activate diffusion, relieve stresses, and homogenize grain structure
Real-time temperature monitoring and feedback control can ensure uniform heating and prevent melting during laser annealing
